items.title: YSR Congress moves Supreme Court alleging candidates blocked from filing nominations for municipal polls
items.summary: The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) has moved the Supreme Court alleging that poll violence blocked its candidates from filing nominations for the upcoming Andhra Pradesh's urban local body elections. The plea challenges an order passed by the Andhra Pradesh High Court refusing to extend the deadline for filing nominations. A vacation Bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana of the apex court will hear the plea on October 21. That is also the last date for withdrawal of candidature. Polling is scheduled for October 28. The party first moved the High Court on October 10, before the polls were notified, seeking secure additional nomination centres. A single-judge dismissed that plea on October 15. Subsequently, it moved the High Court flagging violence at nomination centres and seeking extension of deadline to file nominations. On October 18, a division bench of the High Court comprising Justices Ninala Jayasurya and Purushottam Kumar Chintalapudi rejected the party's plea for a one-day extension to file nominations. The High Court said that the time for filing nominations had expired and any direction to extend the same would amount to interference with the election process. This prompted the plea before the Supreme Court. As per the petition, there was violence at Punganur and Rayachoti on October 16, the first day of nominations. A candidate's papers were snatched and torn at Kadapa, and candidates in Tirupati were assaulted and prevented from reaching nomination centres. Nine Tirupati candidates have filed affidavits saying they were obstructed while trying to file their nominations. The petition argues that the principle of non-interference with elections is only a rule of judicial restraint and not an absolute bar on court's intervention. According to the plea, "In a situation where the democratic process is being thwarted, it is the bounden duty of the Constitutional Courts to step in and ensure that elections take place transparently and that no candidate is forced out of the race." Further, the expiry of time was itself the consequence of the obstruction complained of, and could not be a ground to deny relief, it has been contended. The plea has sought the following reliefs: - extension of the nomination period; - additional nomination centres with videography; - police protection for candidates; and - a stay on unopposed declarations. The petition was filed through advocate Mahfooz A Nazki.

items.title: CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka to remain in custody until October 21
items.summary: A Delhi court on Monday, October 19, extended the judicial custody of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka by two days over an alleged breach of peace bonds. They will remain in custody until their next hearing on October 21. The Delhi police had sought a five-day extension, alleging that the two had breached bonds they furnished on October 11 by calling on people to gather at Jantar Mantar. Police said the site had been de-notified as an official protest venue and alleged that Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka had used social media to mobilise people for demonstrations at other non-designated locations, including Connaught Place, Live Law reported. The CJP leaders were initially detained at an airport on October 10, ahead of protests demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over massive irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. They were released that day after furnishing peace bonds of Rs 50,000 each. They were later detained in connection with an attempt to hold a Tiranga protest at Jantar Mantar and remanded to five days of judicial custody on October 14. Opposing the police request, the defence sought their immediate release and said they would not repeat the alleged conduct. Their lawyers also disputed that the two had called for protests after October 10 and noted that CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke had been released. Special Executive Magistrate Ritu Raj said the police had placed material before the court raising concerns about a possible breach of peace. The court said the men’s assurance that they would not repeat the alleged conduct did not inspire confidence in light of the material presented. “The application filed by the IO [Investigating Officer] is supported by substantial material on record, raising serious concerns regarding the likelihood of breach of peace and disturbance of public tranquillity,” the court said, according to Bar and Bench. The magistrate also rejected the sureties presented for Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, finding them unfit. The order cited a mismatch between a surety’s photograph on the bond and his Aadhaar card, unsatisfactory answers during questioning, and the sureties’ inability to ensure the men’s appearance in court. “The inquiry conducted revealed that both the sureties have no control over the respondents to produce them before the court,” the order said, directing the CJP leaders to provide fresh sureties. items.title: Mangaluru child sexual assault: Church hierarchy knew of allegations weeks before FIR
items.summary: A Catholic priest in Mangaluru, Karnataka, was arrested on Saturday, October 17, for allegedly sexually abusing minor children. Although the arrest comes two days after a First Information Report was registered against the priest, officials of the Mangalore Diocese, including the Bishop, were aware of the allegations for almost two months. Father Cyprian Pinto of St Vincent Ferrer Church in Valencia was arrested by the Mangaluru South police from the residence of his relative, Police Commissioner Sudheer Kumar Reddy said. Father Cyprian faces a case registered under Sections 8 (sexual assault) and 10 (aggravated sexual assault) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, and Section 75(2) (sexual harassment) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023. A community member and an activist told TNM that the matter was brought to the attention of Bishop Peter Paul Saladanha on August 17. Section 19 of the POCSO Act makes it mandatory that any person with knowledge of a sexual offence against a child must bring it to the notice of the authorities. The Public Relations Office of the Mangalore Diocese declined to comment on specific allegations, saying that the matter was being investigated by the police. Meeting with Bishop Satish (name changed), a resident of the neighbouring Udupi district, who has direct knowledge of the events surrounding the alleged abuse, told TNM that five children and their parents met the Bishop on August 17. “These are city boys. They’re much more aware of things. They talked to each other and figured out that they’ve all been abused. They discussed it with the Assistant Parish priest, who’s a young man close in age to the boys. It was this priest who raised the issue with another parish member, who in turn raised the issue in the church, forcing the Vice President to take action. There are a couple of more boys who were abused, but only five boys and their parents eventually came forward to meet the Bishop,” Satish said. Satish said that the visit was arranged by the Vice President of Vincent Ferrer Church Ronald Rodrigues. Asked about this, Ronald Rodrigues declined to comment. “Since a case has been filed, I can’t say anything. If I say anything it will be prejudice (to the case). We can’t confirm anything since it is in the court.” Satish said that each of the five children wrote letters to the Bishop detailing the alleged abuse, but only one got leaked.
